title: Madaniyat va odob: ingliz tilidagi yozilmagan qoidalar
goal_uz: Dars oxirida siz ingliz tilida so‘zlashuvchi muhitda odamlarga to‘g‘ri murojaat qilasiz (Mr/Ms + familiya yoki ism), so‘rovlarni muloyim shaklda aytasiz, noqulay mavzulardan qochib, berilgan noqulay savolni muloyim chetlab o‘tasiz, imo-ishora va shaxsiy masofani hisobga olasiz hamda taklif, sovg‘a va vaqtga rioya bo‘yicha kamida o‘nta “qiling va qilmang” qoidasini tushuntirib bera olasiz.

vocab.uz: bir-biriga ism bilan murojaat qiladigan darajada yaqin bo‘lmoq

scenes.title: Bugun: madaniyat va odob
board: Culture & etiquette in English
Address · Taboos · Body language · Invitations
When in doubt, be more formal (shubha bo‘lsa, rasmiyroq bo‘ling)
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda bahslashishni va fikringizni muloyim, lekin qat’iy himoya qilishni o‘rgandik. Bugun madaniy jihatdan qo‘pol eshitiladigan gaplardan qochishni o‘rganamiz. Grammatik xatoni odamlar kechiradi, madaniy xatoni esa eslab qolishadi. Shuning uchun oltin qoida: shubha bo‘lsa, rasmiyroq va muloyimroq bo‘ling.
scenes.say: Welcome back! Today: how to address people, what not to ask, how close to stand, and how to be a good guest.
scenes.say_uz: Qaytganingiz bilan! Bugun: odamlarga qanday murojaat qilish, nimani so‘ramaslik, qanchalik yaqin turish va qanday yaxshi mehmon bo‘lish.

scenes.title: Unvonlar: Mr, Mrs, Ms, Dr
board: Mr Brown (erkak) · Mrs Brown (turmushga chiqqan ayol)
Miss Brown (turmushga chiqmagan) · Ms Brown /mɪz/ (neytral)
Dr Patel · Professor Jones
UK: Mr, Ms, Dr · US: Mr., Ms., Dr.

examples.t: Good morning, Ms Taylor. Thank you for seeing me.
examples.uz: Xayrli tong, Teylor xonim. Meni qabul qilganingiz uchun rahmat.

examples.t: Dr Patel will see you now.
examples.uz: Doktor Patel sizni hozir qabul qiladi.

scenes.say_native: Birinchi mavzu: murojaat shakllari. Ingliz tilida unvon familiya bilan keladi: “Mr Brown”, “Ms Taylor”. Ayolning oilaviy ahvolini bilmasangiz, “Ms” ni tanlang: ish muhitida bu eng xavfsiz variant. Ilmiy darajasi bor odamga “Dr” deyiladi. Yozuvda Britaniyada odatda nuqtasiz “Mr”, Amerikada esa nuqta bilan “Mr.” yoziladi.
scenes.say: Good morning, Mr Brown. Nice to meet you, Ms Taylor. If you don’t know whether a woman is married, Ms is the safe choice.
scenes.say_uz: Xayrli tong, janob Braun. Tanishganimdan xursandman, Teylor xonim. Ayolning turmushga chiqqan-chiqmaganini bilmasangiz, Ms xavfsiz tanlov.

scenes.title: Qachon ismga o‘tiladi?
board: Please, call me David. (Meni David deb chaqiring.)
What should I call you?
UK & US offices: first names come quickly
No “aka / opa / ustoz” in English
scenes.say_native: Britaniya va Amerikadagi ko‘p ofislarda, hatto rahbar bilan ham, tez ism bilan murojaatga o‘tiladi. Buni odatda katta yoki yuqori lavozimdagi odam taklif qiladi: “Please, call me David.” Bilmasangiz, so‘rang: “What should I call you?” O‘zbekchadagi “aka”, “opa”, “ustoz” ning muqobili yo‘q: kattaga ism bilan murojaat hurmatsizlik emas.
scenes.say: Nice to meet you, Mr Brown. Oh, please, call me David. Thank you, David. And please call me Aziz.
scenes.say_uz: Tanishganimdan xursandman, janob Braun. Iltimos, meni David deb chaqiring. Rahmat, David. Siz ham meni Aziz deb chaqiring.

scenes.title: Murojaatdagi odatiy xatolar
board: ✗ Mr Aziz / Mrs Dilnoza  ✓ Mr Rakhimov / Aziz
✗ Teacher, can I ask?  ✓ Excuse me, Ms Green…
✗ Hey, mister!  ✓ Excuse me! / Excuse me, sir…
scenes.say_native: Uchta odatiy xato. Birinchisi, unvonni ism bilan qo‘shish: “Mr Aziz”. Bu “Aziz aka” ning tarjimasi: yo “Mr Rakhimov”, yo shunchaki “Aziz”. Ikkinchisi, o‘qituvchini “Teacher!” deb chaqirish; ismini ayting yoki “Excuse me” deng. Uchinchisi, notanishga “Hey, mister!” deyish; “Excuse me” yoki “Excuse me, sir” deng.
scenes.say: Excuse me, Ms Green, could I ask a question? Excuse me, sir, I think you dropped your wallet.
scenes.say_uz: Kechirasiz, Grin xonim, savol bersam maylimi? Kechirasiz, janob, menimcha, hamyoningizni tushirib yubordingiz.

scenes.title: Mashq: qanday murojaat qilasiz?
board: 1 An email to Dr Ali Khan, a lecturer you’ve never met
2 Your new manager, Tom Hill, said: “Just call me Tom.”
3 A stranger in the street has dropped his glove
4 A formal letter; you don’t know the person’s name
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta vaziyat. Har biri uchun to‘g‘ri murojaatni ayting. O‘zingizdan so‘rang: ism bilan gaplashishga ruxsat bormi, unvoni nima, ismini umuman bilamanmi? Rasmiy xatda ism noma’lum bo‘lsa, ingliz tilida standart ochilish bor, uni eslang. Javoblarni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: How would you address each person? Think about titles, first names, and what to do when you don’t know the name at all.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir odamga qanday murojaat qilasiz? Unvonlar, ismlar va ism umuman noma’lum bo‘lganda nima qilish haqida o‘ylang.

scenes.title: Javoblar: murojaat
board: 1 Dear Dr Khan,
2 Tom (not Mr Hill any more)
3 Excuse me! / Excuse me, sir!
4 Dear Sir or Madam,
scenes.say_native: Birinchi: “Dear Dr Khan”, unvon va familiya; notanish domlaga “Dear Ali” juda yaqin, “Dear Dr Ali” esa xato. Ikkinchi: shunchaki “Tom”, chunki o‘zi taklif qildi. Uchinchi: “Excuse me!” yoki “Excuse me, sir!” To‘rtinchi: “Dear Sir or Madam”. Ism ma’lum bo‘lsa esa doim ismli shaklni tanlang.
scenes.say: Dear Dr Khan. Tom, have you got a minute? Excuse me, you’ve dropped your glove! Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to enquire about your courses.
scenes.say_uz: Hurmatli doktor Xon. Tom, bir daqiqa vaqtingiz bormi? Kechirasiz, qo‘lqopingizni tushirib yubordingiz! Hurmatli janob yoki xonim, kurslaringiz haqida so‘rash uchun yozyapman.

scenes.title: Muloyim so‘rov: buyruq emas, savol
board: ✗ Give me the report.
Could you send me the report, please?
Would you mind sending me the report? (mind + -ing)
I was wondering if you could… (eng muloyim)

examples.t: Would you mind closing the window?

scenes.say_native: O‘zbekchada “Menga hisobotni bering” normal, chunki ohang yumshatadi. Ingliz tilida buyruq mayli, hatto “please” bilan ham, keskin eshitilishi mumkin. Shuning uchun so‘rovni savolga aylantiramiz: “Could you…?” yoki “Would you mind…?” va “-ing”. Eng muloyimi “I was wondering if you could…”: o‘tgan zamon bu yerda vaqtni emas, hurmat masofasini bildiradi.
scenes.say: Could you send me the report, please? Would you mind closing the window? I was wondering if you could help me with the presentation on Friday.
scenes.say_uz: Hisobotni menga yuborib bera olasizmi? Derazani yopib qo‘ysangiz, qarshi emasmisiz? Juma kungi taqdimotda menga yordam bera olarmikansiz, deb o‘ylagandim.

scenes.title: How are you?, sorry va cheers
board: How are you? → Fine, thanks. And you?
Thanks / Cheers (UK, norasmiy “rahmat”)
Sorry! (urilib ketsangiz, o‘tmoqchi bo‘lsangiz)
scenes.say_native: “How are you?” ko‘pincha salomning bir qismi, haqiqiy savol emas. Javob qisqa: “Fine, thanks. And you?” Sog‘lig‘ingiz haqida batafsil gapirish kutilmaydi. Britaniyada “please”, “thank you” va “sorry” juda ko‘p ishlatiladi: kimdir sizga urilib ketsa, ko‘pincha ikkalangiz ham “Sorry!” deysiz. “Cheers” esa norasmiy “rahmat” ma’nosida ham keladi.
scenes.say: Morning! How are you? Fine, thanks. And you? Not bad, thanks. Could I have a latte, please? Here you go. Cheers!
scenes.say_uz: Xayrli tong! Qalaysiz? Yaxshi, rahmat. O‘zingiz-chi? Yomon emas, rahmat. Bitta latte bera olasizmi? Mana, marhamat. Rahmat!

scenes.title: So‘zma-so‘z tarjima xatolari
board: ✗ I want a coffee.  ✓ Could I have a coffee, please?
✗ You must send it today.  ✓ Would it be possible to send it today?
✗ Repeat, please.  ✓ Sorry, could you say that again?
scenes.say_native: Bu xatolar so‘zma-so‘z tarjimadan chiqadi. Kafeda “I want a coffee” talabchan eshitiladi; “Could I have…?” deng. Hamkasbga “You must” deyish buyruq beradi; “Would it be possible to…?” ancha yaxshi. Ruscha “Повторите, пожалуйста” normal, lekin inglizcha “Repeat, please” keskin tuyuladi: “Sorry, could you say that again?” deng.
scenes.say: Could I have a coffee, please? Would it be possible to send it today? Sorry, could you say that again? I didn’t quite catch that.
scenes.say_uz: Bitta kofe bera olasizmi? Uni bugun yuborishning iloji bormi? Kechirasiz, yana bir bor ayta olasizmi? Yaxshi eshitmay qoldim.

scenes.title: Mashq: muloyim qiling
board: 1 Open the door.
2 Tell me your phone number.
3 I want the bill.
4 Help me with this form.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta keskin gapni muloyim so‘rovga aylantiring. Har birida boshqa shaklni sinab ko‘ring: “Could you…?”, “Could I have…?”, “Would you mind + -ing?” va “I was wondering if…”. To‘rtinchi gapda kattaroq iltimos bor, shuning uchun eng yumshoq variantni tanlang. Savolni yumshoq ko‘tariluvchi ohang bilan ayting.
scenes.say: Make each sentence polite. Use a different structure each time, and save the softest one for the biggest request.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir gapni muloyim qiling. Har safar boshqa tuzilmani ishlating, eng yumshog‘ini esa eng katta iltimos uchun saqlang.

scenes.title: Javoblar: muloyim so‘rovlar
board: 1 Could you open the door, please?
2 Could I have your phone number?
3 Could we have the bill, please?
4 I was wondering if you could help me with this form.
scenes.say_native: Birinchi: “Could you open the door, please?” Ikkinchi: “Tell me” emas, “Could I have your phone number?” Uchinchi: restoranda “Could we have the bill, please?”; Amerikada “the check” deyiladi. To‘rtinchi: “I was wondering if you could help me…” yoki “Would you mind helping me…?” Esda tuting: “please” dan ko‘ra savol shakli muhimroq.
scenes.say: Could you open the door, please? Could I have your phone number? Could we have the bill, please? I was wondering if you could help me with this form.
scenes.say_uz: Eshikni ochib bera olasizmi? Telefon raqamingizni bera olasizmi? Hisobni olib kela olasizmi? Bu shaklni to‘ldirishda menga yordam bera olarmikansiz, deb o‘ylagandim.

scenes.title: Dialog 1: Londondagi ofisda birinchi kun
board: Helen (manager) · James (colleague) · Aziz (new analyst)
Listen: names · a polite request · one awkward question
scenes.say_native: Birinchi dialog. Aziz Londondagi kompaniyada ishining birinchi kunida rahbari Xelen va hamkasbi Jeyms bilan tanishadi. Uch narsaga e’tibor bering: Aziz rahbariga qanday murojaat qiladi va unga nima deyishadi, qanday so‘rov beradi va qaysi savoli noqulay bo‘lib chiqadi. Jeyms bu savolga qanday javob berganini ham eslab qoling.
scenes.say: Helen: Morning! You must be Aziz. I’m Helen Clarke, the team manager. Aziz: Good morning, Mrs Clarke. Helen: Oh, Helen is fine. We all use first names here. This is James. James: Hi, Aziz. Welcome aboard! How was the journey in? Aziz: Fine, thanks, just a bit crowded. Could you show me where the kitchen is? James: Sure. Aziz: By the way, how much do you earn here? James: Ha! Let’s just say it pays the bills. Anyway, help yourself to tea and coffee.
scenes.say_uz: Xelen: Xayrli tong! Siz Aziz bo‘lsangiz kerak. Men Xelen Klark, jamoa rahbariman. Aziz: Xayrli tong, Klark xonim. Xelen: E, shunchaki Xelen deyavering. Bu yerda hammamiz ism bilan murojaat qilamiz. Bu Jeyms. Jeyms: Salom, Aziz. Jamoaga xush kelibsiz! Yo‘l qanday bo‘ldi? Aziz: Yaxshi, rahmat, faqat biroz tirband edi. Oshxona qayerdaligini ko‘rsatib bera olasizmi? Jeyms: Albatta. Aziz: Aytgancha, bu yerda qancha maosh olasiz? Jeyms: Ha! Aytaylik, xarajatlarga yetadi. Xullas, choy va kofeni o‘zingiz olavering.

scenes.title: Mashq: dialog 1 savollari
board: 1 How did Aziz address his manager first?
2 What did Helen ask him to do?
3 Which question was too personal?
4 How did James avoid answering it?
scenes.say_native: Dialogni eslab, to‘rtta savolga javob bering. Birinchi ikkitasi murojaat haqida: Aziz qanday boshladi va rahbar unga qanday ishora berdi. Uchinchisi noqulay mavzu haqida. To‘rtinchisi juda foydali: Jeyms qo‘pollik qilmasdan savoldan qanday qochdi? Uning aniq so‘zlarini eslang, bu ibora sizga ham kerak bo‘ladi.
scenes.say: Answer the four questions. For question four, try to remember James’s exact words.
scenes.say_uz: To‘rtta savolga javob bering. To‘rtinchi savol uchun Jeymsning aynan aytgan so‘zlarini eslashga harakat qiling.

scenes.title: Javoblar: dialog 1
board: 1 Mrs Clarke (title + surname; Ms is even safer)
2 To call her Helen
3 How much do you earn here?
4 Let’s just say it pays the bills. Anyway, …
scenes.say_native: Aziz unvon va familiya bilan boshladi, bu to‘g‘ri; oilaviy ahvolini bilmagani uchun “Ms Clarke” yanada xavfsizroq edi. Xelen ismga o‘tishni taklif qildi, endi “Helen” deyish kerak. Oshxona haqidagi so‘rov a’lo, “Could you…?” shaklida. Maosh haqidagi savol esa noqulay. Jeyms hazil bilan qochdi va “Anyway” deb mavzuni o‘zgartirdi.
scenes.say: Aziz said Mrs Clarke, and Helen asked him to use her first name. James avoided the question about pay with a joke.
scenes.say_uz: Aziz Klark xonim dedi, Xelen esa undan ismi bilan murojaat qilishni so‘radi. Jeyms maosh haqidagi savoldan hazil bilan qochdi.

scenes.title: Taboo mavzular
board: Money: salary, rent, what things cost
Age, weight, appearance (yosh, vazn, tashqi ko‘rinish)
Marriage, children, family plans
Religion & politics (with people you don’t know well)
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi mavzu: taboo mavzular. Yaxshi tanimagan odamdan maosh va narxlar, yosh, vazn va tashqi ko‘rinish, turmush va farzand rejalari, din va siyosat haqida so‘rash shaxsiy hayotga aralashish deb qabul qilinadi. Bular butunlay man etilmagan: yaqin do‘stlar bemalol gaplashadi. Muhimi, kim bilan va qayerda gaplashayotganingiz.
scenes.say: With people you don’t know well, it’s best to avoid questions about money, age, weight, marriage and children, religion and politics.
scenes.say_uz: Yaxshi tanimagan odamlar bilan pul, yosh, vazn, turmush va farzandlar, din va siyosat haqidagi savollardan qochgan ma’qul.

scenes.title: O‘zbekcha g‘amxo‘rlik va xavfsiz mavzular
board: Uzbek: “Uylanganmisiz?” = samimiylik belgisi
English: “Are you married?” = often too personal
Safe: weather, weekend, travel, food, sport, films, work
scenes.say_native: Bizda “Uylanganmisiz? Nechta farzandingiz bor?” degan savollar samimiylik belgisi, ingliz tilida esa ular yangi tanishni noqulay holatga solishi mumkin. Xavfsiz mavzular: ob-havo, dam olish kunlari, sayohat, ovqat, sport, filmlar va ish loyihalari. Ob-havo haqidagi gap suhbatga eshik ochadi. Odam o‘zi oilasi haqida gapirsa, siz ham qiziqish bildiring.
scenes.say: Lovely weather today, isn’t it? Did you do anything nice at the weekend? Are you working on anything exciting at the moment?
scenes.say_uz: Bugun havo ajoyib, shunday emasmi? Dam olish kunlari biror yoqimli ish qildingizmi? Hozir biror qiziqarli ish ustida ishlayapsizmi?

scenes.title: Noqulay savoldan muloyim qochish
board: I’d rather not say, if you don’t mind.
Let’s just say… (aytaylik…)
Oh, that’s a long story!
Anyway, how about you? (mavzuni o‘zgartirish)
scenes.say_native: Noqulay savol berishsa, qo‘pol javob shart emas. “I’d rather not say, if you don’t mind” muloyim, lekin aniq. “Let’s just say…” hazil bilan chetlab o‘tadi. “Oh, that’s a long story!” mavzuni yopadi. Keyin darhol savolni qaytaring: “Anyway, how about you?” Mavzuni o‘zgartirish ingliz tilidagi eng nozik “yo‘q”.
scenes.say: Let’s just say I’m old enough to know better! I’d rather not say, if you don’t mind. Anyway, how about you? Any plans for the summer?
scenes.say_uz: Aytaylik, aqlim kirib qolgan yoshdaman! Agar qarshi bo‘lmasangiz, aytmay qo‘ya qolay. Xullas, o‘zingiz-chi? Yozga biror rejangiz bormi?

scenes.title: Tarjima qilingan “g‘amxo‘rlik” savollari
board: ✗ How much do you earn?  ✓ Do you enjoy working there?
✗ You’ve put on weight!  ✓ You look well!
✗ How much did your flat cost?  ✓ What a lovely flat!
✗ Why aren’t you married yet?  ✓ (don’t ask)
scenes.say_native: “To‘libsiz” ba’zan o‘zbekchada sog‘lik belgisi sifatida aytiladi, ingliz tilida esa “You’ve put on weight” deyarli doim haqorat. “You look tired” ham xavfli: “yomon ko‘rinyapsiz” deb eshitiladi. Narx o‘rniga maqtov ayting: “What a lovely flat!” Maosh o‘rniga ish haqida so‘rang. Turmush haqida umuman so‘ramang: odam xohlasa, o‘zi aytadi.
scenes.say: Do you enjoy working there? You look well! What a lovely flat! How long have you lived here?
scenes.say_uz: U yerda ishlash sizga yoqadimi? Yaxshi ko‘rinyapsiz! Qanday chiroyli kvartira! Bu yerda qancha vaqtdan beri yashaysiz?

scenes.title: Mashq: xavfsizmi yoki xavflimi?
board: 1 What do you do in your free time?  2 How old are you?
3 Who did you vote for?  4 How was your holiday?
5 Is that your natural hair colour?  6 Have you lived here long?
scenes.say_native: Oltita savol. Ularni yangi hamkasbga bera olasizmi? Har biri uchun “safe” yoki “risky” deng. Savolni o‘zingizga berib ko‘ring: notanish odam sizdan buni so‘rasa, noqulay bo‘lasizmi? Xavfli savollar o‘rniga qanday xavfsiz savol berish mumkinligini ham o‘ylang.
scenes.say: Which questions are safe to ask a new colleague, and which are risky? Say safe or risky for each one.
scenes.say_uz: Qaysi savollarni yangi hamkasbga berish xavfsiz, qaysilari xavfli? Har biri uchun safe yoki risky deng.

scenes.title: Javoblar: xavfsiz va xavfli savollar
board: Safe: 1, 4, 6
Risky: 2 (age), 3 (politics), 5 (appearance)
Instead of 3: Have you been following the news?
scenes.say_native: Xavfsiz: birinchi, to‘rtinchi va oltinchi. Bo‘sh vaqt, ta’til va yashash joyi suhbatni yaxshi boshlaydi. Xavfli: ikkinchisi yosh, uchinchisi saylov, beshinchisi tashqi ko‘rinish haqida. Joriy voqealar haqida gapirmoqchi bo‘lsangiz, umumiyroq boshlang: “Have you been following the news?” va suhbatdosh qanchalik ochiq ekanini kuzating.
scenes.say: Free time, holidays and where people live are safe topics. Age, voting and appearance are risky.
scenes.say_uz: Bo‘sh vaqt, ta’til va odamlar qayerda yashashi xavfsiz mavzular. Yosh, saylov va tashqi ko‘rinish xavfli.

scenes.title: Mashq: noqulay savolga javob bering
board: 1 “So, how much do they pay you?”
2 “When are you getting married?”
3 “What do you think of our government?”
scenes.say_native: Endi noqulay savol sizga berildi. Har biriga ikki qismli javob tuzing: avval muloyim chegara yoki hazil, keyin mavzuni o‘zgartiradigan savol. “I’d rather not say”, “Let’s just say…”, “That’s a long story” va “Anyway, how about you?” iboralarini ishlating. Ohang iliq bo‘lsin.
scenes.say: Someone asks you these questions. Answer politely, set a gentle boundary, and change the subject.
scenes.say_uz: Kimdir sizga shu savollarni berdi. Muloyim javob bering, yumshoq chegara qo‘ying va mavzuni o‘zgartiring.

scenes.title: Javob namunalari: muloyim chegara
board: 1 Let’s just say I can’t complain! How’s your new job going?
2 Oh, that’s a long story! Anyway, any holiday plans?
3 I try to keep work and politics separate. How was the conference?
scenes.say_native: Birinchi javobda hazil bor: “I can’t complain”, ya’ni “shikoyat qilolmayman”, raqam esa aytilmadi. Ikkinchisida “That’s a long story” mavzuni yopdi. Uchinchisida aniq, lekin do‘stona chegara: ish va siyosatni aralashtirmaslik. Har uchala javob iliq savol bilan tugaydi, shuning uchun suhbatdosh xijolat bo‘lmaydi.
scenes.say: Let’s just say I can’t complain! Oh, that’s a long story! Anyway, any holiday plans? I try to keep work and politics separate.
scenes.say_uz: Aytaylik, shikoyat qilolmayman! E, bu uzun hikoya! Xullas, ta’tilga biror rejangiz bormi? Men ish va siyosatni alohida tutishga harakat qilaman.

scenes.title: Salomlashish: qo‘l berish va ko‘zga qarash
board: Firm, short handshake + eye contact + smile
Men and women shake hands in business
Eye contact = honesty, confidence
scenes.say_native: Uchinchi mavzu: tana tili. Ish muhitida standart salom: qisqa va mustahkam qo‘l berish, ko‘zga qarash va tabassum. Bizda kattalar oldida ko‘zni pastga olish hurmat bo‘lishi mumkin, u yerda esa ko‘zga qaramaslik ishonchsizlik deb tushuniladi. Diniy sabab bilan qo‘l bermasangiz, bir gap bilan tushuntirish mutlaqo maqbul.
scenes.say: It’s lovely to meet you. I hope you don’t mind, I don’t shake hands for religious reasons, but I’m really glad to meet you.
scenes.say_uz: Tanishganimdan juda xursandman. Umid qilamanki, qarshi emassiz, men diniy sabablarga ko‘ra qo‘l bermayman, lekin siz bilan tanishganimdan chindan xursandman.

scenes.title: Shaxsiy masofa va navbat
board: Personal space ≈ an arm’s length
Less touching with colleagues
Never push in! Sorry, are you in the queue?
UK: queue · US: line
scenes.say_native: Hamkasb yoki notanish bilan gaplashganda odatda taxminan qo‘l uzunligicha masofa saqlanadi. Juda yaqin tursangiz, suhbatdosh orqaga chekinadi. Hamkasbning qo‘lidan ushlab gapirish ham kam uchraydi. Britaniyada navbatsiz kirib olish, ya’ni “pushing in”, katta qo‘pollik. Ishonchingiz komil bo‘lmasa, so‘rang: “Sorry, are you in the queue?”
scenes.say: Sorry, are you in the queue? Excuse me, I think I was next. Oh, no problem, after you.
scenes.say_uz: Kechirasiz, navbatdamisiz? Kechirasiz, menimcha, navbat meniki edi. E, mayli, siz o‘ting.

scenes.title: Imo-ishoralar
board: Thumbs up = good, well done
V-sign with palm facing you = offensive in the UK
Pointing at people = rude → use an open hand
Hand on heart = warm, but may need explaining
scenes.say_native: Bosh barmoqni ko‘tarish “zo‘r, kelishdik” degani. Kaft o‘zingizga qaragan “V” belgisi esa Britaniyada haqoratli; suratga tushganda kaftni tashqariga qarating. Odamga barmoq bilan ishora qilmang, ochiq kaft bilan ko‘rsating. Qo‘lni ko‘ksiga qo‘yish iliq ishora, lekin ko‘pchilik ma’nosini bilmaydi, shuning uchun bir so‘z bilan izohlang.
scenes.say: In Uzbekistan, putting your hand on your heart is a way of showing respect. Oh, that’s a lovely gesture. I didn’t know that.
scenes.say_uz: O‘zbekistonda qo‘lni ko‘krakka qo‘yish hurmat ko‘rsatish usuli. E, bu juda chiroyli ishora. Buni bilmagan ekanman.

scenes.title: Tana tilidagi odatiy xatolar
board: ✗ standing very close  ✓ about an arm’s length
✗ looking down when your manager speaks  ✓ natural eye contact
✗ pushing past people  ✓ Excuse me, could I just get past?
✗ clicking your fingers at a waiter  ✓ eye contact + Excuse me!
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta xato. Juda yaqin turish suhbatdoshni noqulay qiladi. Rahbar gapirganda doim pastga qarash uyatchanlik deb ko‘rinishi mumkin. Tor yo‘lakda indamay o‘tib ketish qo‘pol: “Excuse me, could I just get past?” deng. Ofitsiantni barmoq shiqillatib chaqirish juda hurmatsiz: ko‘z bilan qarang, qo‘lni biroz ko‘taring va “Excuse me!” deng.
scenes.say: Excuse me, could I just get past? Thanks. Excuse me! Could we see the menu, please?
scenes.say_uz: Kechirasiz, o‘tib olsam maylimi? Rahmat. Kechirasiz! Menyuni ko‘rsak bo‘ladimi?

scenes.title: Talaffuz: muloyim ohang va kuchsiz shakllar
board: Sorry? ↗ = Takrorlab yuboring
Sorry. ↘ = Uzr
Could you…? /kʊdʒə/ · Would you mind…? /wʊdʒə maɪnd/
Flat tone = bored or rude
scenes.say_native: Muloyimlikning yarmi ohangda. Ko‘tariluvchi ohangdagi “Sorry?” “eshitmadim, takrorlang” degani, pasayuvchi ohangdagisi esa “uzr”. “Could you” va “would you” tez nutqda bog‘lanib, “kudja” va “wudja” kabi eshitiladi. Tekis, bir xil ohangda aytilgan eng muloyim so‘z ham qo‘pol eshitiladi, shuning uchun so‘rovni iliq ohangda ayting.
scenes.say: Sorry? Sorry, what was that? Oh, sorry, my mistake. Could you help me? Would you mind waiting a moment?
scenes.say_uz: Labbay? Kechirasiz, nima dedingiz? Voy, uzr, mening xatoyim. Menga yordam bera olasizmi? Bir oz kutib tursangiz, qarshi emasmisiz?

scenes.title: Mashq: nima deysiz?
board: 1 You accidentally step on someone’s foot on the bus.
2 People are blocking a narrow corridor.
3 You want to call the waiter.
4 You didn’t hear what your colleague said.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta kundalik vaziyat. Har birida nima deysiz va nima qilasiz? Qisqa, tabiiy iboralarni ishlating, uzun gap kerak emas. To‘rtinchi vaziyatga alohida e’tibor bering: bitta so‘z yetarli, lekin uni to‘g‘ri ohang bilan aytish kerak. Ikkinchi vaziyatda esa so‘rovni kichraytiradigan bitta kichik so‘zni eslang.
scenes.say: What would you say in each situation? Keep it short and natural, and think about your tone.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir vaziyatda nima deysiz? Qisqa va tabiiy gapiring hamda ohangingiz haqida o‘ylang.

scenes.title: Javoblar: kundalik vaziyatlar
board: 1 Oh, I’m so sorry! ↘
2 Excuse me, could I just get past?
3 Eye contact, raise your hand slightly: Excuse me!
4 Sorry? ↗ / Sorry, what was that?
scenes.say_native: Birinchi: pasayuvchi ohangda “Oh, I’m so sorry!” Ikkinchi: “Excuse me, could I just get past?”; bu yerda “just” iltimosni kichraytiradi. Uchinchi: ko‘z bilan qarash, qo‘lni biroz ko‘tarish va “Excuse me!” To‘rtinchi: ko‘tariluvchi ohang bilan “Sorry?” Yolg‘iz “What?” esa qo‘pol eshitilishi mumkin.
scenes.say: Oh, I’m so sorry! Excuse me, could I just get past? Excuse me! Sorry? Sorry, what was that?
scenes.say_uz: Voy, juda uzr! Kechirasiz, o‘tib olsam maylimi? Kechirasiz! Labbay? Kechirasiz, nima dedingiz?

scenes.title: Taklif: haqiqiy va shunchaki xushmuomalalik
board: Real: Would you like to come for dinner on Saturday at 7?
Vague: We must get together sometime!
Accept: I’d love to. What can I bring?
Decline: I’d love to, but I’m afraid I’ve got plans.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtinchi mavzu: taklif, sovg‘a va vaqt. Aniq kun, vaqt va joy bo‘lsa, bu haqiqiy taklif. “We must get together sometime!” esa ko‘pincha shunchaki iliq xayrlashuv. Rad etganda minnatdorlik bildiring va yumshoq sabab ayting. Taklifnomadagi “RSVP” “javob bering” degani: bormasangiz ham xabar berasiz.
scenes.say: Would you like to come round for dinner on Saturday, around seven? I’d love to, thank you! What can I bring? Oh, just bring yourself!
scenes.say_uz: Shanba kuni soat yettilarda kechki ovqatga kelasizmi? Jon deb, rahmat! Nima olib kelay? E, o‘zingiz kelsangiz bas!

scenes.title: Sovg‘a berish va olish
board: To a home: flowers, chocolates, or something from home
Gifts are often opened straight away
Receiving: Oh, you shouldn’t have! It’s lovely.
Business gifts: small; many companies have gift rules
scenes.say_native: Uyga mehmonga borganda kichik sovg‘a olib boriladi: gul, shokolad yoki O‘zbekistondan biror shirinlik. Sovg‘a ko‘pincha darhol ochiladi, uni bir necha bor rad etish shart emas. Ish sovg‘alari kamtarona bo‘lsin: ko‘p kompaniyalarda qimmat sovg‘ani cheklaydigan qoidalar bor, katta sovg‘a pora kabi ko‘rinishi mumkin.
scenes.say: This is for you, just a little something from Uzbekistan. Oh, you shouldn’t have! Can I open it now? It’s beautiful. Thank you so much.
scenes.say_uz: Bu sizga, O‘zbekistondan kichkina sovg‘a. Voy, ovora bo‘libsiz-da! Hozir ochsam maylimi? Juda chiroyli ekan. Katta rahmat.

scenes.title: Vaqtga rioya qilish
board: Work meeting: on time or a few minutes early
Dinner at someone’s home: on time or a little later, never early
Running late? Text the host.
Next day: Thanks again for a lovely evening!
scenes.say_native: Ish uchrashuviga vaqtida yoki bir necha daqiqa oldin keling. Uydagi kechki ovqatga esa erta kelmang: mezbon hali tayyorlanayotgan bo‘lishi mumkin. Kechiksangiz, oldindan xabar yozing. Bizda “yo‘ldaman” deb bir soat kechikish ba’zan kechiriladi, u yerda bu jiddiy ko‘rinadi. Ertasi kuni qisqa rahmat xabari ham yaxshi odat.
scenes.say: Hi Emma, I’m so sorry, I’m running about ten minutes late. The traffic is terrible. See you soon!
scenes.say_uz: Salom Emma, juda uzr, taxminan o‘n daqiqa kechikyapman. Tirbandlik dahshat. Tez orada ko‘rishamiz!

scenes.title: Dasturxon atrofida
board: “No, thank you” = No (taken literally)
Help yourself! (O‘zingiz olavering!)
Yes, please, just a little.
With colleagues: Shall we split the bill?
scenes.say_native: Bizda mehmon ko‘pincha birinchi taklifni rad etadi, mezbon esa “oling, oling” deb qistaydi. Ingliz uyida “No, thank you” so‘zma-so‘z tushuniladi va sizga qayta taklif qilinmasligi mumkin. Xohlasangiz, darhol “Yes, please” deng. “Help yourself” degani “o‘zingiz olavering”. Hamkasblar bilan restoranda esa ko‘pincha hisob bo‘linadi.
scenes.say: Would you like some more? Yes, please, just a little. It’s delicious. Help yourself to the salad. Shall we split the bill? Sure, that’s fine.
scenes.say_uz: Yana olasizmi? Ha, iltimos, ozgina. Juda mazali. Salatdan o‘zingiz olavering. Hisobni bo‘lishamizmi? Albatta, mayli.

scenes.title: Mehmondorchilikdagi xatolar
board: ✗ arriving early for dinner  ✓ on time or a little later
✗ “No, no!” and staying hungry  ✓ Yes, please, just a little.
✗ 40 minutes late, no message  ✓ I’m running late, sorry!
✗ ignoring an RSVP  ✓ replying either way
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta xato bir joyda. Kechki ovqatga yarim soat erta borish mezbonni noqulay holatga soladi. Odob yuzasidan “yo‘q” deb, keyin och o‘tirish faqat sizga zarar. Xabarsiz qirq daqiqa kechikish hurmatsizlik deb qabul qilinadi. Taklifnomaga javob bermaslik mezbonning rejasini buzadi: u qancha ovqat va joy tayyorlashni bilmaydi.
scenes.say: Thank you for the invitation. I’m afraid I can’t make it on Friday, but I hope you have a great evening.
scenes.say_uz: Taklif uchun rahmat. Afsuski, juma kuni kela olmayman, lekin kechangiz ajoyib o‘tishini tilayman.

scenes.title: Dialog 2: Emmaning uyida kechki ovqat
board: Emma (host) · Dilnoza (guest)
Listen: the gift · the shoes · more food · leaving
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi dialog. Dilnoza britaniyalik hamkasbi Emmaning uyiga kechki ovqatga keldi. To‘rt narsani kuzating: u qanday sovg‘a olib keldi, oyoq kiyimi haqida nima deb so‘radi, qo‘shimcha ovqat taklif qilinganda qanday javob berdi va kechani qanday yakunladi. Har bir lahzadagi muloyim iborani eslab qoling.
scenes.say: Emma: Dilnoza, hi! Come in. Dilnoza: Hi, Emma. These are for you, and this is some halva from Tashkent. Emma: Oh, you shouldn’t have! Thank you. Dilnoza: Shall I take my shoes off? Emma: No, don’t worry, keep them on. Emma: Would you like some more lasagne? Dilnoza: Yes, please, just a little. It’s delicious. Dilnoza: Well, I should get going. Thank you for a lovely evening. Emma: Thanks for coming! Let’s do it again soon.
scenes.say_uz: Emma: Dilnoza, salom! Kiring. Dilnoza: Salom, Emma. Bular sizga, bu esa Toshkentdan holva. Emma: Voy, ovora bo‘libsiz-da! Rahmat. Dilnoza: Oyoq kiyimimni yechaymi? Emma: Yo‘q, xavotir olmang, yechmang. Emma: Yana lazanya olasizmi? Dilnoza: Ha, iltimos, ozgina. Juda mazali. Dilnoza: Xo‘sh, men ketishim kerak. Ajoyib kecha uchun rahmat. Emma: Kelganingiz uchun rahmat! Tez orada yana yig‘ilamiz.

scenes.title: Mashq: dialog 2 savollari
board: 1 What did Dilnoza bring?
2 What did she ask about her shoes?
3 How did she accept more food?
4 How did she say goodbye?
scenes.say_native: Dialog bo‘yicha to‘rtta savol. Faktlar bilan birga aniq iboralarni ham eslashga harakat qiling: oyoq kiyimi haqida qaysi modal fe’l bilan so‘radi, qo‘shimcha ovqatni qanday qabul qildi va ketishdan oldin nima dedi. Bu iboralarni mehmonga borganda o‘zingiz ham ishlatasiz.
scenes.say: Answer the four questions, and try to use Dilnoza’s exact phrases.
scenes.say_uz: To‘rtta savolga javob bering va Dilnozaning aynan aytgan iboralaridan foydalanishga harakat qiling.

scenes.title: Javoblar: dialog 2
board: 1 Flowers and halva from Tashkent
2 Shall I take my shoes off?
3 Yes, please, just a little. It’s delicious.
4 I should get going. Thank you for a lovely evening.
scenes.say_native: Dilnoza gul va Toshkent holvasini olib keldi: universal va milliy sovg‘aning yaxshi aralashmasi. Oyoq kiyimi haqida “Shall I…?” bilan so‘radi; uylar har xil, shuning uchun so‘rash eng to‘g‘risi. Ovqatni “Yes, please, just a little” bilan qabul qildi. “I should get going” esa ketishning muloyim shakli.
scenes.say: She brought flowers and halva. She asked, “Shall I take my shoes off?” She said, “Yes, please, just a little,” and finally, “I should get going.”
scenes.say_uz: U gul va holva olib keldi. “Oyoq kiyimimni yechaymi?” deb so‘radi. “Ha, iltimos, ozgina” dedi va oxirida “Men ketishim kerak” dedi.

scenes.title: Mashq: taklifga javob yozing
board: 1 Accept a dinner invitation and offer to bring something.
2 Decline a party invitation politely.
3 Text the host: you’ll be 15 minutes late.
4 Send a thank-you message the next morning.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta qisqa xabar tuzing. Har birida minnatdorlik va aniqlik bo‘lsin. Rad etganda “I’d love to, but…” va “I’m afraid” ni eslang. Kechikish haqidagi xabarda necha daqiqa kechikishingizni aniq yozing. Rahmat xabarida esa bitta aniq tafsilotni maqtang, masalan ovqat yoki suhbatni. Xabarlarni ovoz chiqarib ayting yoki yozing.
scenes.say: Write four short messages: accept, decline, say you’re running late, and say thank you the next day.
scenes.say_uz: To‘rtta qisqa xabar yozing: taklifni qabul qiling, rad eting, kechikayotganingizni ayting va ertasi kuni rahmat ayting.

scenes.title: Javob namunalari: xabarlar
board: 1 I’d love to, thank you! Can I bring anything?
2 Thanks so much for inviting me. I’d love to, but I’m afraid I’m away.
3 So sorry, I’m running about 15 minutes late!
4 Thanks again for last night. The soup was amazing!
scenes.say_native: Birinchisida minnatdorlik va “Can I bring anything?” savoli bor. Ikkinchisida rad etish uch qismdan iborat: rahmat, “I’d love to, but” va qisqa sabab; batafsil bahona shart emas. Uchinchisida aniq vaqt bor. To‘rtinchisida aniq tafsilot: sho‘rva. Bunday kichik detal xabarni rasmiyatchilikdan chin samimiyatga aylantiradi.
scenes.say: I’d love to, thank you! Can I bring anything? I’d love to, but I’m afraid I’m away that weekend. So sorry, I’m running fifteen minutes late! Thanks again for last night. The soup was amazing!
scenes.say_uz: Jon deb, rahmat! Biror narsa olib kelaymi? Borishni juda xohlardim, lekin afsuski, o‘sha dam olish kunlari shaharda bo‘lmayman. Juda uzr, o‘n besh daqiqa kechikyapman! Kechagi kecha uchun yana rahmat. Sho‘rva ajoyib edi!

scenes.title: Yakuniy topshiriq: do‘stingizga maslahat
board: Your friend starts a job in London next month.
Give 5 do’s and don’ts + a reason for each.
Make sure you… · Try not to… · It’s better to… because…
scenes.say_native: Endi navbat sizga. Do‘stingiz kelasi oy Londonda ish boshlaydi. Unga bir daqiqa davomida beshta “qiling va qilmang” maslahatini bering va har birini sabab bilan tushuntiring. Bugungi to‘rt mavzudan kamida bittadan misol bo‘lsin. “Make sure you…”, “Try not to…”, “It’s better to… because…” iboralarini ishlating.
scenes.say: Your turn. Give your friend five do’s and don’ts for working in London, and explain each one with a reason.
scenes.say_uz: Navbat sizga. Do‘stingizga Londonda ishlash bo‘yicha beshta “qiling va qilmang” maslahatini bering va har birini sabab bilan tushuntiring.

scenes.title: Namuna javob: beshta maslahat
board: Use first names once people invite you to.
Try not to ask about salary or marriage.
Make sure you keep an arm’s length and make eye contact.
Don’t arrive early for dinner, and text if you’re late.
scenes.say_native: Mana namunaviy javob. E’tibor bering: har bir maslahat “because” yoki “otherwise” orqali sabab bilan keladi va bugungi to‘rt mavzuni qamrab oladi. Javobingizni solishtiring: sabablar bormi, iboralar har xilmi, ohang do‘stona va ishonchlimi? Bitta mavzu tushib qolgan bo‘lsa, uni qo‘shib, yana bir marta gapirib ko‘ring.
scenes.say: Use first names once people invite you to, otherwise you’ll sound distant. Don’t ask about salary or marriage, because it feels too personal. Keep an arm’s length and make eye contact. And don’t arrive early for dinner, but text the host if you’re running late.
scenes.say_uz: Odamlar taklif qilgach, ism bilan murojaat qiling, aks holda sovuq ko‘rinasiz. Maosh yoki turmush haqida so‘ramang, chunki bu juda shaxsiy tuyuladi. Qo‘l uzunligicha masofa saqlang va ko‘zga qarang. Kechki ovqatga erta bormang, kechikayotgan bo‘lsangiz esa mezbonga xabar yozing.

scenes.title: Xulosa: to‘rt madaniy kalit
board: Address: Mr/Ms + surname → first name when invited
Taboos: money, age, looks, marriage, religion, politics
Body: handshake, eye contact, arm’s length, queue
Invitations: reply, small gift, don’t be early, say “Yes, please”
scenes.say_native: Xulosa. Murojaat: unvon familiya bilan, ruxsat berilgach esa ism. So‘rov savol shaklida. Noqulay mavzular: pul, yosh, tashqi ko‘rinish, turmush, din va siyosat; berilsa, hazil va “Anyway…” bilan qoching. Tana tili: qo‘l berish, ko‘zga qarash, masofa va navbat. Taklifga javob bering, kichik sovg‘a olib boring va erta bormang.
scenes.say: You now know how to address people, make polite requests, avoid sensitive topics, read body language, and behave well as a guest.
scenes.say_uz: Endi siz odamlarga qanday murojaat qilish, muloyim so‘rov berish, nozik mavzulardan qochish, tana tilini tushunish va mehmon sifatida o‘zingizni yaxshi tutishni bilasiz.

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi va keyingi dars
board: Homework: 10 do’s and don’ts + a reason for each
Cover: address · taboos · body language · invitations
Use: Could you…? · Would you mind…? · I was wondering if…
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifasi: o‘nta “qiling va qilmang” qoidasini yozing va har birini bir gap bilan tushuntiring. Mezon: to‘rt mavzuning har biridan kamida ikkita qoida va kamida uchta muloyim so‘rov shakli. Ro‘yxatni iliq ohangda ovoz chiqarib o‘qing. Keyingi darsda PRO 1 modulini yakunlaymiz: yakuniy loyiha va imtihonga tayyorlanamiz.
scenes.say: Write ten do’s and don’ts, each with a short reason. Then read them aloud with a warm, polite tone. See you next time!
scenes.say_uz: O‘nta “qiling va qilmang” qoidasini yozing, har birini qisqa sabab bilan. Keyin ularni iliq va muloyim ohangda ovoz chiqarib o‘qing. Keyingi safar ko‘rishguncha!

homework_uz: Ingliz tilida so‘zlashuvchi mamlakatda ishlaydigan yoki mehmonga boradigan do‘stingiz uchun o‘nta “qiling va qilmang” (do’s and don’ts) qoidasini ingliz tilida yozing va har birini bitta gap bilan tushuntiring (because, otherwise, so that). Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: murojaat va muloyimlik, taboo mavzular, imo-ishora va shaxsiy masofa, taklif, sovg‘a va vaqtga rioya mavzularining har biridan kamida ikkitadan qoida bor; har bir qoidada aniq sabab ko‘rsatilgan; kamida uchta muloyim so‘rov shakli (Could you…?, Would you mind…?, I was wondering if…) ishlatilgan. Keyin ro‘yxatni iliq ohangda ovoz chiqarib o‘qing.

quiz.q: You are writing to a woman called Sarah Jones and you don’t know if she is married. Which greeting is best?
quiz.why_uz: Oilaviy ahvol noma’lum bo‘lsa, Ms + familiya ishlatiladi. Unvon ism bilan qo‘shilmaydi.

quiz.q: Your new manager says, “Please, call me David.” What should you do?
quiz.why_uz: U o‘zi ism bilan murojaat qilishni taklif qildi; endi “David” deyish tabiiy, “Mr David” esa xato.

quiz.q: Which request is the most polite?
options: I was wondering if you could send me the file.
You must send me the file.
quiz.why_uz: I was wondering if you could… eng yumshoq shakl; buyruq va “I want” keskin eshitiladi.
Would you mind dan keyin fe’l -ing shaklida keladi: closing.

quiz.q: Which question is safe to ask a new colleague?
options: Did you do anything nice at the weekend?
quiz.why_uz: Dam olish kunlari xavfsiz mavzu; maosh, turmush va saylov esa juda shaxsiy.

quiz.q: Someone asks how old you are and you don’t want to answer. What is the most natural reply?
options: Let’s just say I’m over thirty! Anyway, how about you?
Why do you ask me this?
quiz.why_uz: Hazil va mavzuni o‘zgartirish muloyim chegara qo‘yadi; qolganlari qo‘pol eshitiladi.

quiz.q: In the UK, which gesture can be offensive?
options: A V-sign with your palm facing you
quiz.why_uz: Kaft o‘zingizga qaragan V belgisi Britaniyada haqoratli; bosh barmoq esa “zo‘r” degani.

quiz.q: You are invited to dinner at a British colleague’s home at 7 pm. When should you arrive?
options: At about 7 or a few minutes later
quiz.why_uz: Uydagi kechki ovqatga erta borilmaydi; vaqtida yoki biroz kechroq kelish odatiy.

quiz.q: The host asks, “Would you like some more?” You want more. What do you say?
quiz.why_uz: “No, thank you” so‘zma-so‘z tushuniladi; xohlasangiz, darhol “Yes, please” deng.

quiz.q: You can’t go to a party. Which reply is best?
options: Thanks so much for inviting me. I’d love to, but I’m afraid I’ve got plans.
quiz.why_uz: Muloyim rad etish: minnatdorlik + I’d love to, but… + I’m afraid + qisqa sabab.
